verdict.rationale: Supabase Auth documents its own Custom Access Token Hook for adding or changing claims in the JWT, and documents that the Auth token scopes database access row by row through RLS policies. Together these surface authorization data in tokens and enforce it. However, the evidence shows no first-party role or permission definition model: developers must build roles in their own tables. A community member also asked which external AuthZ provider (e.g., Cerbos or Casbin) to pair with it. Missing for 10: built-in role/permission definition and management, documented RBAC guide showing role claims enforced end-to-end, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can define roles and permissions and have them enforced and surfaced in session tokens for authorization checks

citations.quote: You can use a [Custom Access Token Hook](/docs/guides/auth/auth-hooks/custom-access-token-hook) to add, remove or change claims present in the token.
The Auth Token scopes database access on a row-by-row level when used along with [RLS policies](/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security).
You can connect this data to your own tables using triggers and foreign key references.
